scope: Proposition 15.1 (Full-perimeter minimizing enclosures) of the manuscript “Equality and rigidity in the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Equality-and-rigidity-in-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f1aab59ba484eb8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 119-120. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The minimum of Pg over A exists and equals ag(B) > 0. Every minimizer has a regular representative whose frontier T is a nonempty compact embedded C1,1 hypersurface, smooth and minimal on T \ B. Its graph functions are locally W2,∞, hence W2,2, including at contact with B. Its outward coorientation points toward a connected exterior containing the asymptotic end. All minimizing frontiers lie in one compact subset of X. Every frontier is a C1 and area limit of smooth full enclosing cuts in int X. If HB < 0 for the normal into X, every minimizer contains a fixed exterior collar of B. Its frontier is then a smooth minimal full cut, and its closed exterior is smooth, connected, complete with its 119 nonempty boundary included, and one-ended. Its boundary is outer area-minimizing there, with every component counted.
